packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-12 - FIRST READING FROM IMAGES ONLY (UNVERIFIED)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
this leaf or an earlier reading of it. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001.jpg
to image-010.jpg of this packet. I did nothing beyond the rules. I make no
attempt to name work or author.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)

- Two overviews: image-001.jpg (face A) and image-006.jpg (face B). Tiles
  image-002..005 cover face A top to bottom; image-007..010 cover face B top to
  bottom. Neighbouring tiles overlap by one to three lines.
- A narrow vertical strip, about 4 cm wide by the scale bar and about 14 cm
  tall, upright as photographed. A hard vertical crease with small holes
  (sewing or fold line) runs down the written area on both faces and hides one
  to three letters on most lines.
- The strip preserves part of one text column plus an intercolumnar or marginal
  blank and the very edge of a neighbouring column:
  * Face A: the main column is on the right; its line beginnings are intact and
    its line ends are cut off by the right edge. At the far left edge are the
    last one or two letters of lines from another column, with brown diagonal
    hatch strokes beside them.
  * Face B: the main column is on the left; its line beginnings are cut off by
    the left edge and its line ends are intact. At the far right edge are the
    first strokes of lines from another column, ending in a circled dot at the
    foot.
  So the leaf had at least two columns per face. Top margin blank on both faces
  (about 3 cm), so line 1 on each face looks like the first line of the column.
- About 29 lines of the main column survive on each face.
- Script: small, compressed Gothic book hand (textualis), dark brown to black
  ink, heavily abbreviated, with superscript letters.
- Colour: on face A a blue paraph within the text (image-005 line 4) and a blue
  stroke over/under the end of the line above it. On face B one short phrase
  written in red within a line (image-008 line 9) and a red paraph or red touch
  at image-010 line 4. Thin brown diagonal hair-strokes are scattered over the
  text on face A (pen trials or line fillers; they are not letters).
- A black paraph-like sign stands inside image-004 line 9.
- On face B a ruled ink line runs under the left part of image-008 line 10 and
  another under the last line (image-010 line 8); a short stroke underlines the
  end of image-009 line 9.
- No running title, no enlarged initial, no gloss visible. The upper left of
  face A carries only faint grey offset or show-through, not readable.

Tentative interpretation (not observation): continuous prose with numbered
scriptural references ("gen. 28", "Io. a.") and paraphs marking new points.
I infer nothing further.

2. SPANS SELECTED

Both main columns were read in full as far as the cut and the crease allow
(face A lines 1-29, face B lines 1-29). Unread: the stubs of the neighbouring
columns at the outer edges (single letters only) and the offset at the top of
face A.

Conventions: (?) follows an uncertain reading; ( ) holds a proposed expansion;
[illegible] = ink present but not readable; [...] = lost at the cut edge;
[crease] = letters hidden in the fold; 7 = Tironian et; 9 = the con-/-us sign;
superscripts are written ^x. Abbreviation strokes are rendered by the expansion
in parentheses where I could propose one.

3. FACE A, main column (line ends cut at the right edge)

image-002.jpg (text begins about halfway down the tile)
 1  i(n) paup^te(?) (paupertate?) exi(st)e(n)te(?) . q^a(?) [...]
 2  7 debitis obligat[...]
 3  su(n)t paup(er)[es?] 7 [hole] alien[...]
 4  solu(er)e debitu(m) 7 tol[...]
 5  ati(?) a g(rati)a(?) p(ar)adysi . [...]
 6  (cut by tile edge; = image-003 line 3)

image-003.jpg (lines 1-2 repeat image-002 lines 4-5)
 3  ip(s)o mori^t(?) (or mort^uo?) 7 sp(?)e[...]
 4  tu(m)(?) 7 ip(su)m adiuit(?) in(?)[...]
 5  p(ar)adysu(m) ut sic m[...]
 6  gen(esis?) . 28(?) . D(?)[illegible]tu^r(?) [...]
 7  ubi(?) dicc(?) lo[hole]^tur(?) ge(?)[...]
 8  a debitis 7 adiut(?)[...]
 9  q(uo)d d(icitu)r 7 alr(?) (aliter?) inuen(?)[...]
10  ho(min)ib9(?) recip(?)[crease]ller(?)[...]
11  lig(?)ei^nos(?) 7(?) inuen(?)[...]
12  dim9(?) 7 ce[illegible]si^m(?) [...]

image-004.jpg (lines 1-2 repeat image-003 lines 11-12)
 3  mu(n)di q(uo)s(?) 9fer(?)it(?)[...]
 4  n3 7 ip(s)e i(n) c[illegible]ce(?) (cruce?) q[...]
 5  i(n) deb(i)tu(m)(?) mu(n)di e(st)(?) sat(?)[...]
 6  cc(?)ia t(?)m^na(?) rechat(?) [...]
 7  to(?) [black paraph-like sign] Q(?)^e uenit(?) . i(?) . [...]
 8  ligat(i)o(?) dy^bli(?) (dyaboli?) illi(?)[...]
 9  g(rati)e(?) 7 debi[crease] solu(?)[...]
10  reuert(er)et(?) [crease, hole] ad(?) [...]
11  io(?) . a . mod(?)[crease] q(?)e[...]

image-005.jpg (lines 1-2 repeat image-004 lines 10-11; a blue stroke runs
under the end of line 2)
 3  me [blue paraph] 7(?) uid(?)e[crease]t(?) a(?)[...]
 4  q(uo)s(?) mu(n)du(m) relir(?)[...]
 5  sta(?) illo^r(?) (illorum?) uoc(?)[crease]' bn(?)[...]
 6  tat^ua(?) ei9 q(?) p(?) uen(?)[...]
 7  i(n) p(?)le(?) ut sic dicat(?)[...]
    (last line; parchment ends just below, traces of yellow at the edge)

Left-edge stubs on face A (ends of lines of another column): isolated letters
only, e.g. "3" (image-002, level with line 2), "u" or "ii" (image-002, level
with line 5), "e" (image-004, level with line 7). Not readable as words.

4. FACE B, main column (line beginnings cut at the left edge)

image-007.jpg (text begins about halfway down the tile)
 1  [...]ata(?) sa[crease]cipiu(n)t(?) d^r(?)
 2  [...]ir(?)c(?) [crease]a(?) 9sol(ati)o(n)em(?)
 3  [...]t(?) ce[hole] despic(er)e(?) 7 p(?)
 4  [...]y(?) ad [crease]sol(ati)o(n)em(?) uelut(?) .

 6  (cut by tile edge; = image-008 line 3)

image-008.jpg (lines 1-2 repeat image-007 lines 4-5)

 4  [...]o uin(?)[crease]c(?)il' e(st)(?) p(?)m^i(?)

10  [...]alis(?) [crease] [in red:] [illegible]tia p(ar)tit(?)
11  [...]t mu(n)du(m) 7c(etera) . Vn(?) lig'(?)
    (a ruled ink line under the left part of this line)
12  [...]n' illa(?) [crease] cor.r.ectio (points between the letters as written)

image-009.jpg (lines 1-2 repeat image-008 lines 11-12)
 3  [...]t ord(?)[hole]ne(?) rep(re)he(n)de(?)
 4  [...] p'mo(?) (primo?) d3 (debet) i(n) sp(irit)uali(?) des(?)
 5  [...]c sp(irit)ual(?)[crease]s mod9 d^r(?) x(?)
 6  [...] du(?)[crease]ollio(?) q^ia(?) ie(?)
 7  [...]elat(?)[crease] sp(iritu)m(?) s(an)c(tu)m(?) i(n)
 8  [...]o(?) ey(?)[crease]3 sig(?) . i' . d^r(?) (short underline beneath the end)
 9  [...]sp(?)[illegible] [crease] debe(n)t(?) re
10  [...]o^t(?) gui(?)[hole]e mu(n)du(m) etc(?)
11  [...] h'(?) de[crease]ate'(?) q . s . s .

image-010.jpg (lines 1-2 repeat image-009 lines 10-11)
 3  [...]cat(?) [crease] lib(er)tate(m) 7
 4  [...] uin(?)[red paraph or red touch]q(uo)s(?) itaq(ue)
 5  [...] tag(?)[crease] cet(er)i(?) . i' . dictu(m)(?)
 6  [...]ore(?) [crease]o h(abe)bitis(?)
 7  [...]cta(?)l[crease][illegible]tur(?) s(an)c(tu)s(?) .
    (a ruled ink line under the left part of this line)
 8  [tops of letters of one further line at the torn lower edge; illegible]

Right-edge stubs on face B (beginnings of lines of another column): single
strokes or letters down the whole height (e.g. "c", "r", "i", "q", "g"), ending
in a circled dot at the foot (image-010). Not readable as words.

5. LIMITATIONS

- Every line is incomplete: face A lacks its line ends, face B its line
  beginnings, and the crease removes one to three letters mid-line on both
  faces. Roughly half of each original line survives, so no sentence is whole.
- Firmest readings on face A: "7 debitis obligat", "solu(er)e debitu(m) 7 tol",
  "a g(rati)a p(ar)adysi", "p(ar)adysu(m) ut sic m", "gen. 28", "a debitis 7",
  "q(uo)d d(icitu)r 7", "mu(n)di", "7 ip(s)e i(n)", "io. a. mod", "mu(n)du(m)",
  "ut sic dic".
  Firmest readings on face B: "9sol(ati)o(n)em" (twice), "despic", "alueo",
  "7 mittit", "7 uos", "cap(er)e sp", "mu(n)du(m) 7c", "cor.r.ectio",
  "rep(re)he(n)de", "mod9", "mu(n)du(m)", "lib(er)tate(m) 7", "itaq", "h(abe)bitis".
  Everything else is a letter-shape proposal.
- The number after "gen." is read 28 with some doubt (the second digit could be
  another figure). The reference in image-004 line 11 is read "io. a." (a book
  abbreviation followed by a letter); the first sign could also be the numeral 10.
- The red words in image-008 line 10 are partly in the crease; only the endings
  "-tia" and a word beginning with p and an abbreviation stroke are visible.
- Which face is recto is not determinable from the images, nor the order of the
  two columns relative to each other.
- A flattened image of the crease and the neighbouring strip of the same leaf
  (if it survives) would be needed to complete the lines.
